reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Reconstructed the three years and choice slots from the adopted EER table and checked the eligibility and proposal rules. Separately reread workbook evidence for the repaired courses and the strongest related methods, compared it with exact external component roles, and checked final schedules, content fields and source links.
findings: The adopted Maastricht FASoS EER Article 3.6.1 pages 15–18 supplies 180 EC: 96 elementary, 54 specialisation and 30 graduation. Year one includes 1 EC compulsory mentoring. Later mentoring is optional and zero credit. The chosen period-four pair is Othering Europe and Analysing Arts II; period five is Power and Democracy and Doing Conceptual Analysis II. Both pairs are in semester four. The arts analysis choice uses 3 EC and relates to the programme’s arts focus. For either 4 EC methods alternative, its extra credit counts toward the 30 EC semester-five elective space. Year three includes 30 EC approved open study in semester five, then Doing Research in Arts and Culture and the English research proposal at 7 EC each and the 16 EC English thesis. The English research and writing, proposal and thesis choices are consistent with Article 3.3.1.

Article 4.2 requires positive binding study advice (45.5 first-year credits) before year two, all 60 first-year credits before year three, and all 60 first-year plus at least 45 second-year credits before the thesis. The proposal result is retained only if the thesis is passed in the same academic year. Article 3.8 permits approved minors, external courses, internships and other options subject to route-specific restrictions and academic approval. The example preserves open space and excludes noncompulsory mentoring, internships, honours and study abroad from compulsory credit claims.

The regional sustainability project is possible in the first term and supplies team enquiry with a regional partner. Documentary methods strengthen environmental representation while retaining a digital media role. The digital plan retains the economics of automation and uses Creative Communication Laboratory for actual critical and artistic work. Qualitative Research Methodology explicitly includes ethnography and participant observation. Researching the American Century develops question formulation and source criticism and supports a partial research-course relationship. It is a historical course, and its substantial paper is distinct from the dedicated proposal and required Maastricht thesis.
